events.category: DMV cultural crossover / world premiere / 50th-season opener
lineup: Black Alley — live music for the Chanel DaSilva world premiere
events.factual_description: The Washington Ballet presents Go-Go 50 at Warner Theatre in Washington, DC from Friday, October 30 through Sunday, November 1, 2026. The official calendar lists four performances: October 30 at 7:30 PM, October 31 at 2:00 PM and 7:30 PM, and November 1 at 2:00 PM. The mixed program opens The Washington Ballet's 50th season and includes Trey McIntyre's Blue Until June to music by Etta James, Choo San Goh's Configurations to music by Samuel Barber, Edwaard Liang's The Art of War to music by Michael Torke, and a world premiere by Chanel DaSilva featuring live music by D.C.'s Black Alley. The Washington Ballet describes the new work as bridging classical ballet with the legacy of Go-Go and rooting the collaboration in Washington's culture and sound. Ticketmaster independently lists all four performances and confirms Warner Theatre; the October 30 event page states 6:30 PM doors and a 7:30 PM show. Accessible Ticketmaster pages do not expose a stable numeric single-ticket face value, so official price fields remain null rather than using group-sales pricing.

en.why_it_matters: This is one of those D.C. ideas that becomes more interesting because the city itself is part of the instrumentation: The Washington Ballet is opening its 50th season with a Chanel DaSilva world premiere powered live by Black Alley, putting classical movement in direct conversation with Go-Go rather than using Washington culture as decoration. The anniversary frame matters, but the live collision of forms is the real reason to make room for it.
en.trip_verdict: For the DMV, make room for one of the four Warner Theatre performances and choose the time that fits the weekend; there is no reason to chase geography when the cultural point of the piece is Washington itself. The three-day run also gives enough flexibility to treat this as a strong local plan rather than a brittle one-night scramble.

es.why_it_matters: Ésta es una de esas ideas de D.C. que se vuelve más interesante porque la ciudad misma forma parte de la instrumentación: The Washington Ballet abre su temporada 50 con un estreno mundial de Chanel DaSilva impulsado en vivo por Black Alley, poniendo el movimiento clásico en conversación directa con el Go-Go en vez de usar la cultura de Washington como decoración. El aniversario importa, pero el verdadero motivo para hacerle espacio es el choque vivo entre esos dos lenguajes.
es.trip_verdict: Desde el DMV, le haría espacio a una de las cuatro funciones del Warner Theatre y escogería la que mejor embone con el fin de semana; no tiene sentido perseguir otra geografía cuando el punto cultural de la pieza es precisamente Washington. Las cuatro funciones en tres días dan además suficiente flexibilidad para convertirlo en un buen plan local sin volverlo una carrera por una sola noche.
